report: One real split: the distributed protasis subordinator. DEU.22.7 gives lema'an both of the ASV's 'that's and leaves its waw only the 'and'; DEU.22.2 does the opposite, folding 'or if' onto the second waw as a rule 55 coordinator-plus-subordinator pair. Rule 55's closing paragraph names DEU.22.2 verbatim as the case it excludes ('gives *or* to the second waw and both *if*s to the one 'im'), and the chapter's own recorded convention says the same. Patched: 'im (s002) now holds t002 and t011 headed on t002, the waw (s009) holds only t010 'or'. No other verse is touched, and no BSB comparison changes.

Checked and found licensed by the source, not split: 'any man' divided at DEU.22.8 (article present, rule 41) but whole on the noun at DEU.22.13 (no article, rule 15); 'the father of the damsel' (22.15, 22.19) against 'the damsel's father' (22.16, 22.29), which is rule 29's anarthrous-versus-possessive count and follows the ASV's own word order; the attributive article rendered by a relative (22.22, 22.25, 22.29) against the prenominal rendering at 22.27, which rule 41 decides on where the ASV puts the attributive; beit as rectum with 'of' at 22.21 s008 and as adverbial accusative with a supplied 'in' at s029; shenehem taking 'of them' at 22.22 and a bare 'them' at 22.24, each the pronoun the ASV wrote. Every demonstrative phrase in the chapter (22.14, 16, 18, 20, 24, 26) divides the same way: demonstrative takes the one determiner, noun article and agreement article both unrepresented.

The chapter's three recorded conventions hold everywhere they apply: 'to death' for the consequent wa-met with its waw unrepresented (22.21, 22.24) beside the finite 'then they shall die' at 22.22; 'lay ... to charge' with the dative le- taking 'to' at 22.14 and the verb holding it whole with the italic pronoun added at 22.17; 'the tokens of' as supplied completion headed on 'virginity' in all five occurrences.

The seven added units are consistent with one another: supplied object pronouns with no object morpheme (22.4 'them', 22.17 '*her*', 22.19 'them'), the supplied measure noun '*shekels*' at 22.19 and 22.29 with 'of' left on kesef under rule 33, the supplied possessive 'thy' at 22.7 where no suffix is written against the suffix-borne 'his' at 22.19, and the supplied subordinator 'that' at 22.20 where no conjunction stands in the clause.

BSB: no genuine error. The R x 13 and Td x 11 groups are the documented convention difference — BSB attaches a recast preposition and an unrendered agreement article to their phrases. The named singletons are each right on the ASV as written: 22.3 hh (no object pronoun in 'thou hast found'), 22.14 we- (the clause opens bare), 22.21/22.24 wa- (the recorded 'to death' convention), 22.19 'ot (bare object after 'fine him'), 22.22 gam (the ASV writes no 'also'; 'both' answers to the numeral), 22.26 nefesh (unrendered in 'and slayeth him'). Nothing was adjusted to improve the rate.

Left standing with the verse's own note under rule 8, not re-litigated: DEU.22.17 'and yet' read as one connective rendering of the single waw (competing reading marks 'yet' added under rule 51); DEU.22.4 'help' read as the rendering of 'immo (competing reading leaves the preposition unrepresented and 'help' added); DEU.22.24 'being in' read as rule 49's supplied copula on the reduced locative clause. Each is a single occurrence with no second verse to be inconsistent with.

No promotion and no new convention. The one defect this chapter produced was a failure to apply a rule the contract already states with this very verse as its worked example, and the chapter log already records the same judgment, so new text would say twice what is said once.
